title: Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016
currency: TO VERIFY: the provided file is the original 2016 text. Later amendments (believed to include 2018 and 2019) are not in the file.

scope.applies_to: All persons who generate, collect, receive, store, transport, treat, dispose or handle bio-medical waste, including hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, dispensaries, veterinary institutions, laboratories, blood banks, health and vaccination camps and first aid rooms of schools.

definitions.text: A person having administrative control over the institution and the premises generating bio-medical waste, including a hospital, nursing home, clinic, dispensary, veterinary institution, animal house, pathological laboratory, blood bank, health care facility and clinical establishment.

key_rules.text: Occupier shall not give treated bio-medical waste with municipal solid waste.
Occupier hands over segregated waste per Schedule I to a common bio-medical waste treatment facility (CBWTF).
No on-site treatment facility where a CBWTF service is available within seventy-five kilometres.
No untreated bio-medical waste shall be mixed with other wastes.
Transport only by the CBWTF operator in labelled vehicles meeting SPCB conditions and the Motor Vehicles Act.
Untreated human anatomical, animal anatomical, soiled and biotechnology waste not stored beyond forty-eight hours.

colour_categories.content: Human and animal anatomical waste, soiled waste, expired or discarded medicines, chemical waste, microbiology and lab waste
colour_categories.treatment: Incineration, plasma pyrolysis or deep burial; others as per Schedule I

colour_categories.content: Contaminated recyclable waste: tubing, bottles, IV sets, catheters, urine bags, syringes without needles, gloves
colour_categories.treatment: Autoclave or microwave or hydroclave, then shredding; to authorised recyclers or energy recovery. Not to landfill.

colour_categories.content: Waste sharps including metals: needles, syringes with fixed needles, scalpels, blades
colour_categories.treatment: Autoclave or dry heat sterilisation, then shredding or encapsulation

routing_implications.summary: Bio-medical waste is collected by the CBWTF operator, never by municipal door-to-door vehicles. Hospitals and clinics appear in municipal routes only for their general solid waste. SWM Rules 2026 r. 5(1)(k) repeats that it must not be mixed with solid waste.
routing_implications.household_overlap: Used needles, syringes and expired medicines from households are SWM special care waste (SWM r. 3(1)(zx)), collected via deposition centres.
